title: Alcubierre 1994: the warp drive metric
hook: A bubble of contracted and expanded space that carries a ship past light speed, paid for in negative energy.
text: the claim within general relativity, and without wormholes or any change of topology, there is a spacetime in which a ship travels between two stars a distance $d$ apart and comes home in a time that can be made as short as you like, as measured by clocks on the ship and by clocks on the stars alike. the ship never moves faster than light locally. it sits at rest inside a small region of flat space, a "bubble", and the bubble is carried along by a distortion of spacetime itself: space contracts ahead of it and expands behind it, in the same way that comoving observers in an inflating universe separate faster than light without either of them ever leaving its light cone. the ship's world line is a timelike geodesic. its proper time equals coordinate time, so there is no time dilation relative to home, no proper acceleration and, if the bubble wall is sharp and larger than the ship, negligible tidal force at the ship. the spacetime is globally hyperbolic, so it contains no closed causal curves. the proposal does not claim that this spacetime can be built. alcubierre says plainly that the metric violates the weak, dominant and strong energy conditions, that the matter needed is "exotic" in the same sense as the matter that holds a wormhole open, and that the only known licence for negative energy density is quantum field theory, for instance the casimir effect. the claim is narrower and stronger than the press has ever made it: general relativity, taken as a theory of geometry,

title: Bobrick and Martire 2021: physical warp drives
hook: A classification that says every warp drive is a moving shell of matter, and a subluminal positive-energy class whose one worked example turns out to be flat space.

title: Einstein–Rosen bridge (1935)
hook: The two-sheeted "bridge" in the Schwarzschild solution: the first wormhole in the literature, and one that no signal can cross.
text: the claim einstein and rosen were not proposing a shortcut. they were trying to build elementary particles out of pure field, with no singularities anywhere, using only the metric of general relativity and the maxwell potential. their move was to take the schwarzschild solution, change the radial coordinate so that the horizon at $r = 2m$ becomes the neck $u = 0$ of a surface with two identical sheets, and read the neck as the particle: physical space is "a space of two identical sheets, a particle being represented by a 'bridge' connecting these sheets" . a many-particle world would be two sheets joined by many bridges, and because nothing is singular the field equations would fix both the field and the motion of the particles. stated as generously as possible, the bridge is the simplest possible wormhole: two asymptotically flat regions joined at a throat of finite area, obtained from the vacuum einstein equations with no extra ingredients, no exotic matter and no new fields. every later wormhole in this catalogue, from wheeler's geons and foam to morris and thorne 1988 to er = epr, descends from this picture. what the bridge does not claim, and never did, is that anything can get from one sheet to the other. that question was settled by fuller and wheeler in 1962, and the answer is no. the bridge belongs at the top of the l3 list because it is the object everyone else modifies, and because its failure mode, the throat pinching off before light can cross, is the cleanest

title: The EM drive
hook: A closed, tapered microwave cavity claimed to push itself without exhaust at a millinewton per kilowatt; the most careful measurement finds nothing above the photon-pressure floor, and the claim would have broken momentum conservation, not the light barrier.

title: Entanglement signalling and the no-communication theorem
hook: Every "entanglement radio" and quantum ansible, and the theorem that closes them: measuring one half of an entangled pair changes nothing that the other half can see.

title: ER = EPR (Maldacena and Susskind 2013)
hook: The conjecture that every entangled pair is joined by an Einstein–Rosen bridge, and why that bridge carries no messages.
text: the claim maldacena and susskind, "cool horizons for entangled black holes", fortsch. phys. 61, 781 (2013), start from a fact and make a conjecture. the fact: the eternal black hole in anti-de sitter space, whose two exterior regions are joined by an einstein–rosen bridge, is the gravity dual of the thermofield double state, a particular maximally entangled state of two copies of the boundary theory. "these solutions can be interpreted as maximally entangled states of two black holes that form a complex epr pair" . the conjecture: "we suggest that similar bridges might be present for more general entangled states" , and in the body of the paper the authors "take the radical position that in a theory of quantum gravity they are inseparably linked, even for systems consisting of no more than a pair of entangled particles" (§3). einstein–rosen bridges and einstein–podolsky–rosen correlations are the same thing seen from two sides: er = epr. the paper is written against the firewall paradox of almheiri, marolf, polchinski and sully. two distant black holes joined by a bridge are an existence proof of a black hole maximally entangled with a distant system that nevertheless has a smooth horizon, and the authors use that to argue the interior of an old black hole is built out of its entanglement with its own hawking radiation. that is the claim's real content. for this catalogue the relevant part of the claim is its self-imposed limit, which the authors state before anything else.

title: Everett and Roman 1997: the superluminal subway
hook: The Krasnikov tube in four dimensions: its negative-energy bill, its Planck-thin walls and the time machine two tubes make.

title: Fell and Heisenberg 2021: positive energy from hidden geometric structure
hook: A Helmholtz split of the shift vector that turns Eulerian energy density into a sum of principal minors, and a superluminal example that is positive for those observers only.
text: the claim shaun fell and lavinia heisenberg ask whether a compact superluminal soliton in plain general relativity can be generated by positive energy densities only, and answer that within one subclass of shift-vector spacetimes it can, at least as the eulerian observers see it. their tool is a decomposition. split the shift vector into a gradient part and a divergence-free part. the hamiltonian constraint then separates into a term built from the second-order principal minors of the hessian of the potential, a cross term, a term that is never positive and a curl term. in the purely irrotational sector the energy density is just the sum of the three minors, which has a geometric reading: positivity is a statement about the convexity of the potential in each two-dimensional subspace. that reading makes it "a relatively simple matter" to write down configurations with positive semi-definite eulerian energy, and explains why the classical drives fail: alcubierre uses one component of the shift, so only the negative terms survive, and natário's divergence-free shift is purely solenoidal, for which the energy is never positive. they exhibit two superluminal configurations. the first is a piecewise potential with a central shift of magnitude 1.3 and positive energy, which they set aside because its corners are not physical. the second is a twice-differentiable potential built from gaussians and error functions with a central shift of about 1.26, everywhere positive eulerian

title: Fuchs et al. 2024: the constant-velocity physical warp shell
hook: A matter shell of two Jupiter masses carrying a small shift vector, satisfying every energy condition, subluminal and at constant velocity: the one positive-energy warp result still standing.

title: Gain-assisted superluminal light propagation
hook: A light pulse crossing a caesium cell with a negative group index leaves before it arrives, undistorted, by classical interference in anomalous dispersion; its front still travels at exactly c.
text: the claim the paper makes a precise and modest claim, and the faster-than-light reading that the press attached to it is a different claim, so both are stated here. wang, kuzmich and dogariu (nature 406, 277, 2000) claim that in a region of anomalous dispersion created between two closely spaced raman gain lines in caesium vapour, a laser pulse propagates with a group velocity that exceeds $c$ and is in fact negative, while its shape is preserved and its intensity is neither strongly absorbed nor strongly amplified. their measured group-velocity index is $n_g = -310 \pm 5$, so that the peak of a pulse appears at the exit of the cell before it enters, an advance of about 62 ns for a cell 6 cm long. this is the best-controlled demonstration of a negative group velocity, cleaner than the absorptive cases where the transmitted pulse is heavily attenuated and reshaped. the authors say plainly that the effect is "not at odds with causality, being a direct consequence of classical interference between its different frequency components in an anomalous dispersion region" . the ftl reading, made in 2000 by press accounts and by some proponents of signalling schemes, is that a pulse which leaves before it arrives has carried something faster than light and could carry a message. in its strongest form: the pulse is undistorted, so any information encoded in its shape is available at the exit 62 ns early, and a chain of such cells could compound the advance without limit. the dossier

title: Gott's cosmic-string time machine (1991)
hook: Two infinitely long cosmic strings passing each other fast enough let an observer circle them and arrive in their own past, with no exotic matter anywhere.
text: the claim gott, phys. rev. lett. 66, 1126 (1991), presents "exact solutions of einstein's field equations ... for the general case of two moving straight cosmic strings that do not intersect" . a single straight cosmic string is a conical defect: spacetime is flat everywhere except on the string, from which a wedge of angle $8\pi g\mu$ has been cut out and the edges glued. a single string cannot make a time machine. but when two parallel strings move past each other in opposite directions, each fast enough that $\gamma_s > (\sin 4\pi\mu)^{-1}$ in the laboratory frame (units $g = c = 1$), the solution "show[s] closed timelike curves (ctc's) that circle the two strings as they pass, allowing observers to visit their own past" . the same happens for non-parallel strings and for point masses in (2+1)-dimensional gravity . in its strongest form the claim is that closed timelike curves need neither a wormhole nor negative energy. cosmic strings are ordinary matter satisfying the weak energy condition; the spacetime is topologically minkowski, free of singularities and horizons (carroll, farhi, guth and olum §i). the device is nothing but two lumps of positive-energy matter moving quickly, and general relativity, taken at its word, permits it. gott himself flagged the limit: for finite string loops, black-hole formation may prevent the closed curves from forming . the catalogue files the construction under l3 because it is the wormhole-free member of the time-machine family: the

title: The Hartman effect and the Nimtz tunnelling claims
hook: A tunnelling wave packet's delay stops growing with barrier thickness, so its apparent speed can exceed c without limit; the delay turns out to be a lifetime, not a transit time, and no signal beats light.
text: the claim a quantum particle, or an electromagnetic wave, can pass through a region it is classically forbidden to enter: a potential barrier higher than its energy, a waveguide narrower than its cutoff, an air gap between two prisms at total internal reflection, a photonic band gap. inside the barrier the wave is evanescent, its wavenumber is imaginary and its amplitude decays rather than oscillates. hartman showed in 1962 that the time a gaussian wave packet appears to spend crossing a rectangular barrier, computed from the peak of the transmitted packet, becomes independent of the barrier thickness once the barrier is opaque. divide a thickness that can be made as large as you like by a delay that does not grow and you get an apparent traversal velocity that exceeds $c$ and has no upper bound. every experiment done since, at optical, microwave and acoustic frequencies, confirms the delay saturation. günter nimtz and his collaborators take the next step. since 1992 they have argued that the measured delays are genuine traversal times, that evanescent modes therefore cross barriers in zero time, that the only delay is a universal scattering time at the barrier entrance of order one period of the carrier, and that this is a superluminal signal velocity, not merely a superluminal group velocity. nimtz and stahlhofen's 2007 preprint puts it at its strongest: evanescent modes "lie outside the bounds of the special theory of relativity", they are the optical counterpart of

title: Heim theory and the Dröscher-Häuser propulsion proposal (2004 to 2005)
hook: A 12-dimensional quantised "poly-metric" with six interactions, a photon-to-gravitophoton converter and an integer-indexed parallel space with light speed nc; conference papers, no derivations, no reproduction.

title: Kaluza-Klein and the hyperspace reading (Kaluza 1921, Klein 1926, ADD 1998, Randall-Sundrum 1999)
hook: Extra dimensions in physics are compact, warped or both, share the light cone of ordinary space and turn motion "in the fifth dimension" into mass; nothing in them is a separate space with its own rules.
text: the claim this is a negative dossier, so two claims need stating and keeping apart. the physics claim, in its strongest form, is that spacetime may have more than four dimensions and that this explains things four dimensions cannot. kaluza showed in 1921 that five-dimensional general relativity in vacuum, with nothing depending on the fifth coordinate, contains four-dimensional gravity and maxwell's electromagnetism together. klein showed in 1926 that if the fifth dimension is a circle of planck-scale circumference, momentum around it is quantised and appears as electric charge, which is why nobody has seen the extra dimension. arkani-hamed, dimopoulos and dvali (add) argued in 1998 that the weakness of gravity "on distances $\gtrsim 1$ mm is due to the existence of $n \ge 2$ new compact spatial dimensions large compared to the weak scale", with the standard model "localized to a 4-dimensional manifold of weak scale 'thickness' in the extra dimensions" (add 1998, abstract). randall and sundrum showed in 1999 that a single warped extra dimension, "a slice of $\mathrm{ads}_5$ spacetime", generates the weak scale from the planck scale "through an exponential hierarchy" (randall and sundrum 1999, abstract). these are exact solutions of the higher-dimensional einstein equations and are graded as such. the hyperspace claim is what fiction needs and is the thing this dossier scores: a second space, reachable at will from any point in ours, with its own metric in which the distance

title: Passage through the Kerr interior (Carter 1968)
hook: The analytically extended rotating black hole has a ring you can fly through into another universe; the real interior has a wall of infinite blueshift where the map runs out.
text: the claim the kerr solution describes the spacetime outside a rotating mass. carter, phys. rev. 174, 1559 (1968), worked out its global structure: the maximal analytic extension, the causal behaviour, and, thanks to an unexpected fourth constant of motion, the complete integration of every geodesic . the proposal graded here is the one that fell out of that map and was repeated for fifty years in textbooks and fiction: a rotating black hole is not a dead end. the singularity is a ring, not a point. an infalling body that crosses the outer horizon, then the inner (cauchy) horizon, can avoid the ring, pass through the disc it bounds into a region of negative radial coordinate, or continue to a new exterior region: "all geodesics which do not reach the central ring singularities are complete" . only geodesics confined to the equatorial plane hit the ring at all . in its strongest form the claim is that a sufficiently massive spinning black hole is a tunnel whose far end opens onto another asymptotically flat universe, and the trip is a free fall with survivable tides. the claim, stated in full, has always carried the warning that carter attached to it. the extended manifold contains closed timelike curves, "there are closed timelike lines which are not removable by taking a covering space", and if the spin or charge exceeds the mass so that the horizons vanish, "it is possible to connect any event to any other by a future-directed timelike line" . what the claim did not carry

title: Krasnikov 1998: the tube laid on the way out
hook: A metric laid along the outbound flight makes the return arbitrarily short by the home clock, for negative energy.

title: Lentz 2021: hyper-fast positive-energy solitons
hook: The claim that a superluminal warp soliton can be sourced by positive energy and a conducting plasma, and the two independent analyses that found it was never a solution at all.
text: the claim erik lentz's paper says that the twenty-five-year link between superluminal warp bubbles and negative energy was an artefact of the shapes people had tried. alcubierre used a single component of the shift vector; natário used a divergence-free shift. both choices force the eulerian energy density (the energy density seen by observers falling freely normal to the flat time slices) to be negative wherever the bubble wall has structure. lentz proposes a third family: take the shift vector to be the gradient of a potential, and make that potential obey a hyperbolic wave equation on the spatial slice instead of a linear or elliptic relation. for such "hyperbolic" solitons the energy density can be written as a product of the wave-equation source and its own integrated gradient, and a rule can be stated that keeps it non-negative everywhere: arrange the sources so that the local source density and the source gradient integrated back along the wave cone always share a sign. he exhibits a configuration of rhomboid-shaped sources in a pentagonal arrangement whose central region carries a level shift vector, so that a payload there rides along at the soliton's speed with proper time equal to coordinate time and negligible tidal force, and reports that the energy density is positive everywhere so the weak energy condition is satisfied, that the eulerian momentum density vanishes and that the trace of the einstein equations is consistent with a plasma of massive fluid plus

title: Lorentz-violating frameworks (the Standard-Model Extension and Hořava-Lifshitz gravity)
hook: Effective field theories with a preferred frame, in which a particle species may have its own maximal velocity without an antitelephone; every coefficient measured so far is consistent with zero.
text: the claim the claim is not that anything travels faster than light. it is that lorentz invariance might be an approximate symmetry, exact in the low-energy world we test and broken at some scale by physics we do not yet have, and that the breaking can be parametrised in a theory that is otherwise ordinary quantum field theory. the standard-model extension (sme) of colladay and kostelecký is "a general lorentz-violating extension of the minimal su(3) × su(2) × u(1) standard model including cpt-even and cpt-odd terms", which "can be viewed as the low-energy limit of a physically relevant fundamental theory with lorentz-covariant dynamics in which spontaneous lorentz violation occurs" (colladay and kostelecký 1998, abstract). it keeps gauge invariance, energy-momentum conservation, hermiticity and power-counting renormalisability, and it keeps covariance under observer transformations while breaking it under particle transformations. every coefficient in it is a background tensor field, fixed in some frame, that particles feel and observers do not. hořava's 2009 proposal does the same thing to gravity from the other end. it is "a candidate quantum field theory of gravity with dynamical critical exponent equal to $z = 3$ in the uv", power-counting renormalisable in 3 + 1 dimensions, in which "the effective speed of light, the newton constant and the cosmological constant all emerge from relevant deformations of the deeply nonrelativistic $z = 3$ theory at short distances"

title: The Mach effect thruster
hook: Woodward's proposal that a body whose internal energy fluctuates while it accelerates fluctuates in mass, and that a piezoelectric stack can turn that into propellantless thrust; the most sensitive balances find vibration, not thrust.
text: the claim james woodward's proposal rests on mach's principle in sciama's form: inertia is the gravitational action of all the matter in the causally connected universe on a body that is accelerated. take that seriously as a field theory, write the gravitational potential of the universe as $\phi \approx c^2$ at every point, and the wave equation for $\phi$ sourced by a body whose proper energy density changes in time acquires transient source terms. woodward reads those terms as a transient change in the body's rest mass: any object that absorbs or releases internal energy while it is being accelerated fluctuates in mass, by an amount proportional to the second time derivative of its energy density, plus a smaller term, always negative, proportional to the square of the first derivative. the fluctuation is tiny at ordinary power levels but grows with frequency, and woodward's thruster is a device to exploit it: a stack of piezoelectric discs driven at tens of kilohertz so that its internal energy oscillates, arranged so that the stack pushes a mass forwards while the mass is heavier and back while it is lighter, giving a net time-averaged force with no propellant expelled. woodward reports thrusts of order a micronewton at a few hundred volts in the early devices and of order tens to a hundred micronewtons in the niac-funded designs of 2017 to 2018, and argues that the momentum is exchanged with the distant matter of the universe through the gravitational field, so that no

title: Maldacena, Milekhin and Popov: traversable wormholes in four dimensions (2018), and the humanly traversable sequel (2021)
hook: A pair of near-extremal magnetic black holes joined by a throat that charged fermions hold open with Casimir energy; it is longer inside than the road outside.
text: the claim maldacena, milekhin and popov, arxiv:1807.04726, published class. quantum grav. 40, 155016 (2023), "present a wormhole solution in four dimensions. it is a solution of an einstein maxwell theory plus charged massless fermions. the fermions give rise to a negative casimir-like energy, which makes the wormhole possible" . two magnetically charged black holes of opposite charge, each near extremality, are joined at the bottom of their throats. in the magnetic field a massless charged fermion has a zero-energy lowest landau level of degeneracy $q$, the integer flux, so one four-dimensional fermion becomes $q$ massless two-dimensional fermions running along the field lines. in the wormhole those field lines close into circles, a massless fermion on a circle has negative casimir energy, and that negative energy, fed into the einstein equations, is what an ordinary einstein–maxwell throat lacks to stay open. "we should emphasize that this wormhole does not require any exotic matter. in fact, the ordinary matter of the standard model is enough!" (§9.1). the standard model embedding uses weak hypercharge and works if the whole configuration is smaller than the electroweak scale, so the 2018 wormholes are microscopic (§8). the paper is as clear about the limit as about the result: "it is a long wormhole that does not lead to causality violations in the ambient space" . "by 'long' we mean that it takes longer to go through the wormhole than through the ambient space" (§1).

title: Meta relativity (Bilaniuk, Deshpande and Sudarshan 1962)
hook: The classical extension of special relativity to particles created above c: imaginary rest mass, a single-sheeted energy surface and the reinterpretation principle for negative energies.

title: Morris–Thorne traversable wormhole (1988)
hook: The metric that made wormholes a subject: a horizon-free throat held open by matter whose tension exceeds its energy density.
text: the claim morris and thorne, am. j. phys. 56, 395 (1988), reverse the usual order of general relativity. instead of choosing matter and solving for the geometry, they write down the geometry a traveller would want, a static spherically symmetric tunnel between two asymptotically flat regions with no horizon and tolerable tides, and let the einstein equations tell them what matter would have to thread it. the answer is a "new class of solutions of the einstein field equations ... which describe wormholes that, in principle, could be traversed by human beings" . the design brief was carl sagan's contact, which thorne was asked to make consistent with the laws of physics, and the paper is framed as a tool for teaching relativity. in its strongest form the claim is this. nothing in the einstein equations forbids a throat that stays open. the only thing forbidding it is the matter: at the throat the material must carry a radial tension $\tau_0$ larger than its own energy density $\rho_0 c^2$, which "no known material" does and which "would violate all the 'energy conditions' that underlie some deeply cherished theorems in general relativity" . but quantum field theory already violates those conditions in small ways (the casimir effect), so "it is not possible today to rule out firmly the existence of such material" . given that material, the paper shows that the throat can be made large enough and the redshift gentle enough that a human passes through in comfort, in a time of

title: Morris, Thorne and Yurtsever: the wormhole time machine (1988)
hook: Take one mouth of a traversable wormhole on a fast round trip and the shortcut becomes a machine for visiting your own past.
text: the claim the paper, phys. rev. lett. 61, 1446 (1988), makes a conditional claim and is careful about the condition: "if the laws of physics permit an advanced civilization to create and maintain a wormhole in space for interstellar travel, then that wormhole can be converted into a time machine with which causality might be violatable" . the conversion uses nothing but special relativity applied to the two mouths. carry one mouth away at high speed and bring it back; its clock, being the clock of a travelling twin, lags the clock of the stationary mouth. but the wormhole's throat is short, so the two mouths remain nearly simultaneous through the tunnel. the result is a permanent offset between "through" and "around", and once the offset exceeds the external light travel time between the mouths, a traveller who goes through and comes back around arrives before leaving. as its best proponent would put it, the claim is a theorem about wormholes, not a recipe for paradox. it says that the physics of traversable wormholes cannot be separated from the physics of closed timelike curves, so that whoever wants the shortcut must also want, or forbid, the time machine. the paper also asks whether the exotic matter can exist at all, and turns the question into one about whether quantum field theory enforces an averaged version of the weak energy condition: "whether wormholes can be created and maintained entails deep, ill-understood issues about cosmic censorship, quantum gravity, and

title: Natário 2002: warp drive with zero expansion
hook: The general warp drive class, and a member of it that neither contracts nor expands space and still needs negative energy.
text: the claim the usual story of the alcubierre drive, that space is contracted ahead of the bubble and expanded behind it and that the bubble moves in response, is not what makes it work. natário's claim is that a warp drive is any globally hyperbolic spacetime built from flat euclidean slices with unit lapse and a time-dependent shift vector field $x$ on euclidean 3-space, and that the bubble moves because $x$ carries it: the region where $x$ vanishes (the interior) slides through the region where $x$ equals the ship's velocity (the exterior, in ship-fixed coordinates), and whether space ahead is contracted or not is a detail of the particular $x$. to prove it, he constructs a divergence-free $x$, so that the expansion of the eulerian volume elements is identically zero everywhere, and shows the resulting spacetime carries a ship at arbitrary speed exactly as alcubierre's does. along the way he proves that every non-flat member of the class violates the weak or the strong energy condition, gives the general formula for the energy density on flat slices, and shows that any member with $v_s > 1$ has a horizon, a visibility horizon and infinite blueshift at the horizon, whatever the choice of $x$. the claim is therefore two things: a definition and a counterexample. the definition has become the standard one; the register's wrp-1 entry adopts it and santiago, schuster and visser's 2022 theorem is proved for it. the counterexample removes the heuristic without removing the bill.

title: The OPERA superluminal neutrino (2011)
hook: A 60 nanosecond early arrival over 730 km that became a 6.5 nanosecond null result once a fibre connector was reseated and an oscillator recalibrated; corrected, not retracted.
text: the claim on 22 september 2011 the opera collaboration posted a measurement of the time of flight of muon neutrinos from the cern neutrino beam to gran sasso (cngs) over a baseline of about 730 km. the abstract of that first version reported "an early arrival time of cngs muon neutrinos with respect to the one computed assuming the speed of light in vacuum of $(60.7 \pm 6.9\ (\mathrm{stat.}) \pm 7.4\ (\mathrm{sys.}))$ ns", corresponding to $(v - c)/c = (2.48 \pm 0.28\ (\mathrm{stat.}) \pm 0.30\ (\mathrm{sys.})) \times 10^{-5}$ (arxiv:1109.4897v1). in its strongest form the claim was not "neutrinos are faster than light" but "we have measured this, with systematic and statistical errors we have controlled, and we cannot find the mistake"; the collaboration wrote that it intended to continue investigating possible systematic effects and invited scrutiny. a six-sigma effect in a well-instrumented experiment is a claim of fact about an instrument before it is a claim about nature. read as physics, the anomaly would have meant lorentz invariance violation in the neutrino sector at the level of 25 parts per million, since the neutrino's rest mass gives a deviation below $10^{-19}$ at these energies. every theoretical response took that as the hypothesis, and one of them (cohen and glashow) showed it was inconsistent with the beam having arrived at all. origin and lineage the measurement was a by-product: opera was built to see tau neutrinos appear in a muon neutrino beam, and

title: The relativistic rocket
hook: The sublight alternative: hold one gravity of acceleration and the crew reaches Proxima in three and a half years, the galactic centre in twenty, by their own clocks; the price is a mass ratio that grows exponentially with the destination.
text: the claim a ship that accelerates at a constant one gravity by its own instruments never exceeds the speed of light, yet by its own clock it can cross any distance in the galaxy within a human lifetime, because time dilation grows without bound as the ship approaches $c$. special relativity does not forbid interstellar travel; it forbids returning to the era you left. this is the control group of the catalogue: every other physics entry is a scheme to beat this ship, or a real effect read as one. the proposal is not that the ship is fast for the people left behind, since it arrives later than light would, but that the crew's proper time is short, and that a civilisation willing to spend energy on a heroic scale could send people to the stars with the physics we have. the strongest form of the claim adds the engineering. sänger's photon rocket, which converts mass to light and throws it backwards, is the ideal exhaust; the bussard ramjet, which scoops interstellar hydrogen and fuses it, would remove the need to carry fuel at all; marx's laser-pushed vehicle, which leaves the engine at home, would remove the reaction mass from the ship. sagan argued in 1963 that with these, "no fundamental energetic problems exist for relativistic interstellar spaceflight" and that at one gravity all points in the galaxy are accessible within the lifetime of a human crew (abstract, via secondary record). origin and lineage the kinematics are in einstein's 1905 paper and were made explicit as

title: Retrocausal signalling proposals
hook: Delayed-choice and quantum-eraser schemes in which switching a distant interference pattern on and off would send a message backwards in time; the fringes and the anti-fringes always add to nothing.
text: the claim quantum mechanics has delayed-choice experiments. in wheeler's version an experimenter's later choice of measurement decides whether a photon that has already passed a two-slit screen behaved as a wave or a particle. in the entangled versions of the 1990s the choice is made on the photon's twin. dopfer's 1998 innsbruck experiment showed that the interference pattern behind a double slit for photon 1 appears or disappears depending on where the detector for its momentum-entangled twin, photon 2, is placed: at the focal plane of a lens, where the twin's momentum is measured and which-slit information is erased, fringes appear; at the image plane, where the twin's position reveals which slit, they do not. kim, yu, kulik, shih and scully's delayed-choice quantum eraser of 2000 does the same with the erasing choice made after photon 1 has been detected. in all of these the fringes appear only in the coincidence counts, that is, in photon 1's data after it has been sorted by photon 2's results. the retrocausal signalling proposal is the observation that photon 2's detector can be anywhere, arbitrarily far away and arbitrarily late, and the question whether the coincidence sorting can be dispensed with. if alice, holding photon 2, can decide by moving her detector whether bob, holding photon 1, sees fringes or not, and if bob can see this in his raw singles counts without waiting for alice's data, then alice's choice is a bit that bob reads at once, and, because alice can

title: The Scharnhorst effect
hook: Light crossing the gap between Casimir plates travels a fraction of order $10^{-32}$ faster than c for micron plates, because the vacuum it crosses has been made emptier than empty; the effect is real, unmeasurable and causally harmless.
text: the claim the speed of light in vacuum is a property of the vacuum. quantum electrodynamics describes light propagating through a sea of virtual electron-positron pairs, and the two-loop correction to photon propagation depends on the state of that sea. between two parallel conducting plates the vacuum is modified: the casimir boundary conditions remove modes and lower the zero-point energy density below its free-space value. scharnhorst calculated in 1990, and barton confirmed by a different route the same year, that photons propagating perpendicular to the plates therefore see an effective refractive index slightly less than one and travel at a speed $c_\perp$ slightly greater than $c$, while photons parallel to the plates travel at $c$. the effect scales as the inverse fourth power of the plate separation and is, for any separation that could be built, far too small to measure. in its strongest form the claim is that this is a genuine change in the propagation speed of light in a physical vacuum, not a group-velocity or tunnelling artefact, and that at high frequency the signal velocity is modified as well. the faster-than-light reading, which the papers themselves do not make, is that here at last is a physical mechanism that makes signals exceed $c$, so that the causality consequences of cau-1 follow and, in principle, an experiment could exploit them. liberati, sonego and visser took that reading seriously as a test case and showed that it does not lead to causal

title: Tachyons (Feinberg 1967)
hook: Feinberg's Lorentz-invariant field theory of particles that were never below c, and why its quanta turned out to be an instability rather than a courier.
text: the claim special relativity forbids accelerating a massive body through the light barrier. it does not, on its face, forbid a particle that was created already above c and stays there. feinberg's 1967 paper takes that gap seriously. it asks whether a relativistic particle with spacelike four-momentum, always faster than light in vacuum, can be given a consistent quantum field theory, and answers yes for the free, spinless case. he named such particles tachyons. the paper does not claim they exist. it claims that their existence is not excluded by relativity, that they could be produced in pairs without anything crossing the light barrier and that the way to settle the question is experiment. the strongest form of the claim has three parts. first, kinematics: a particle with $p^\mu p_\mu < 0$ has a velocity $v = pc^2/e$ greater than c in every inertial frame, can never be brought below c and loses energy as it speeds up. second, consistency: the negative-energy states that appear when such a particle is viewed from a suitably boosted frame are to be read as positive-energy antiparticles moving the other way, the reinterpretation principle inherited from bilaniuk, deshpande and sudarshan. third, quantisation: a scalar field with negative mass-squared can be quantised so that its fourier modes with real frequency describe free tachyons, and the theory built this way is lorentz invariant even though, as feinberg notes, the vacuum and the particle number are not. one thing

title: Van Den Broeck 1999: the pocket geometry
hook: A femtometre bubble around a neck to a 200 m pocket cuts the warp bill from universe scale to a few solar masses.
text: the claim the quantum-inequality bill for an alcubierre bubble is enormous because the total negative energy scales as $r^2/\delta$: a macroscopic bubble radius $r$ divided by a planck-scale wall thickness $\delta$. van den broeck's claim is that the bubble radius and the size of the room inside it are different things. multiply the spatial part of the alcubierre metric by a conformal factor $b^2(r_s)$ that is huge inside a tiny radius and equal to one outside it, and you get a warp bubble whose outer surface is a few femtometres across while the flat region inside it, the "pocket", is two hundred metres in diameter. ford and pfenning's own formula then gives the wall a negative energy of about $-6 \times 10^{29}$ kg instead of $-6 \times 10^{62}$ kg; the transition region between pocket and bubble adds about $-1.4 \times 10^{30}$ kg of negative energy and $4.9 \times 10^{30}$ kg of positive energy; and the quantum inequality is checked and found to hold with a margin of more than an order of magnitude. the total negative mass is "of the order of a few solar masses", which "puts the warp drive in the mass scale of large traversable wormholes", and the new geometry keeps every advantage of the original: the pocket's centre moves on a timelike geodesic with proper time $t$, weightless and without time dilation. the author is careful about what this does not show. it is "a proof of principle concerning the total energy required", not a realistic proposal: the energies are

title: Visser's thin-shell wormholes (1989)
hook: Cut a hole in two copies of flat space, glue the edges together, and the exotic matter collapses to a sheet at the throat that a traveller need never touch.
text: the claim visser, phys. rev. d 39, 3182 (1989), takes the traversable wormhole of morris and thorne and strips it to the bone. remove an identical compact region from two copies of minkowski space and identify the boundaries. the result is a spacetime that is flat everywhere except on the junction surface, which is the throat, and all the curvature and all the matter live there as a delta function. two things follow that spherical symmetry had hidden. first, the throat need not be a sphere: any shape will do, and a cube with flat faces is the natural example. second, on a flat face the surface stress-energy vanishes, so "it is possible for a traveller to traverse such a wormhole without passing through a region of exotic matter" . the traveller feels "no forces, tidal or otherwise, during the trip" and is "simply shunted into the other universe" . the paper does not claim to have removed the exotic matter, and says so in the abstract: "as in previous analyses, the weak energy condition is violated in these traversable wormholes" . its claim is that the exotic matter can be minimised and quarantined, pushed to the edges of a polyhedron, and that its total amount is set by geometry alone, independent of the size of the wormhole. it also supplies the simplest proof in the literature that a convex throat must violate the energy conditions: the throat acts as a perfect mirror into the other universe, so a convex throat defocuses light, and the focusing theorem says defocusing

title: Warp drives in modified gravity
hook: Torsion, conformal gravity and other extensions move the warp bill from the matter side of the field equations to the geometry, and what each move costs.
text: the claim every theorem that prices a warp drive in negative energy is a theorem about the source of general relativity: the einstein equations turn a statement about geometry (light rays converge) into a statement about matter (energy density is positive), and the warp metrics violate the geometric statement. the claim of this family of proposals is that general relativity is the wrong theory to price the drive with. gravity has been tested where torsion, higher-curvature terms and extra scalar fields are negligible; in a theory that agrees with einstein's everywhere it has been tested and differs where curvature or spin density is extreme, the same alcubierre metric can be sourced by matter that obeys the energy conditions, because the extra sector absorbs what in general relativity would have to be negative. two peer-reviewed papers make this claim with worked mathematics. debenedictis and ilijic (2018) show that in einstein-cartan gravity, general relativity supplemented with torsion coupled to spin, the alcubierre and van den broeck metrics can be sourced by a weyssenhoff spin fluid whose stress-energy satisfies the weak and null energy conditions everywhere, with the ship still in free fall since torsion vanishes outside matter. varieschi and burstein (2013) show that in mannheim's conformal (weyl) gravity, a fourth-order theory, the alcubierre metric with a suitable shaping function has non-negative energy density for every eulerian observer at speeds up to about

title: Wheeler's geons and quantum foam (1955–1962)
hook: Where the word "wormhole" came from: Wheeler's programme of building matter, charge and multiply connected space out of nothing but geometry and fields.
text: the claim wheeler's geometrodynamics asked whether everything could be geometry. a geon, phys. rev. 97, 511 (1955), is a lump of electromagnetic radiation held together by its own gravity for a time long compared with its period: "a completely classical, divergence-free, self-consistent picture of the newtonian concept of body" over masses from about $10^{39}$ g to $10^{57}$ g . it is mass without mass: the gravitational mass comes entirely from the energy of the field, with no material source. misner and wheeler, ann. phys. 2, 525 (1957), then added charge without charge (the rotating case, the kerr interior passage, was treated by wheeler's group as a wormhole of the same family): electric field lines threading a handle in a multiply connected space look, from outside, like a positive charge at one mouth and a negative charge at the other, with no charge anywhere. they gave the handle its name, "wormhole" . wheeler's companion paper, ann. phys. 2, 604 (1957), argued that at the planck scale the vacuum should be a quantum foam in which such handles form and dissolve continually, so that multiply connected topology is not exotic but the default texture of space . as a proposal about faster-than-light travel the claim is deliberately modest and, in its strongest form, is a question rather than an assertion: if space is multiply connected, then between two points there are alternative routes, and "one may ask if a signal traveling at the speed of light along one route could be

title: White et al. 2021: the worldline-numerics Casimir pattern
hook: A DARPA-funded numerical study of Casimir energy around a micron pillar, whose plot resembled the Alcubierre toroid and was reported as the first real warp bubble.
text: the claim harold white and four co-authors were modelling custom casimir cavities for a darpa project on vacuum energy storage. the cavity of interest is a pair of parallel plates about 4 µm apart with 1 µm pillars along the mid-plane, designed to test white's "dynamic vacuum model", which predicts that the negative casimir energy density in a cavity is not uniform but concentrated along the mid-plane, and that this structure comes with a small electrostatic field that a high-impedance oscilloscope could see as a transient voltage. the engineering question was whether a pillar would screen itself from that field. to answer it the team implemented worldline numerics, a monte carlo method for casimir energies developed by gies, langfeld and moyaerts, validated it on plate-plate and plate-sphere cases and ran it on the plate-pillar geometry. the paper's claim is what they saw when they plotted the result. the negative energy density around the pillar, in a two-dimensional section, "was observed to be qualitatively quite similar to a two-dimensional representation of energy density requirements for the alcubierre warp metric": a lenticular concentration of negative energy either side of a central body, which in the alcubierre case is the toroidal ring of negative density around the flat interior. a toy model of a 1 µm sphere in a 4 µm cylinder gave a three-dimensional toroidal casimir density that "correlates well with the alcubierre warp metric requirements". on that basis the

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968): the Star Gate
hook: A slab left on a moon of Saturn that opens into a switching station for the galaxy; Clarke's novel and Kubrick's film show the passage and refuse to explain it.
text: the drive as depicted the star gate is the second half of the monolith. arthur c. clarke's novel and stanley kubrick's film were written together in 1964 to 1968, and they diverge in where the gate is and how much is said about it, so both are described here. in the novel, the tycho monolith's radio burst is aimed at japetus, a moon of saturn (clarke's spelling), and discovery is sent there . on the white plain of japetus bowman finds a monolith two kilometres tall, which the novel calls big brother and then, as he descends towards it in the pod, the star gate . his last transmission to earth is the line that everybody knows, ending "it's full of stars!" (chapter 39, "into the eye") . chapter 40, "exit", has the gate open and close; chapter 41 is titled "grand central", because what bowman sees on the far side is a vast enclosed space through which other things are passing, and which he reads as a switching station, a junction on a network of gates . he is carried on through an alien sky, close by a red giant and its white dwarf companion, and set down in a hotel room built from television broadcasts (chapters 42 to 44), where he sleeps, ages, is remade as the star-child and returns to earth's orbit . the passage is a passage: bowman is inside the pod throughout, does nothing to steer and is delivered. in the film, the destination is jupiter, not saturn, because kubrick and douglas trumbull could not make rings they were satisfied with . the final act is titled "jupiter and

title: The Alderson drive (Niven and Pournelle 1974)
hook: Tramlines between stars along lines of equal thermonuclear flux, an instantaneous jump from one Alderson point to another, and a crew too dazed afterwards to fight.
text: the drive as depicted the mote in god's eye (larry niven and jerry pournelle, simon and schuster, 1974) is the defining instalment, though the drive belongs to pournelle's wider codominium setting . the novel states the rule in chapter 4, "priority oc": the alderson drive's pathways "are generated along lines of equipotential thermonuclear flux", which is to say that between two stars whose fusion output defines a line of equal potential there is a tramline, and a ship at the right point on it (the alderson point) can switch on the drive and appear, with no elapsed time, at the corresponding point in the other system (read in an online copy of the text). the prologue names the same tramline effect as what colonised the stars and made interstellar war possible . not every pair of stars has a tramline, not every tramline is usable and the points lie well outside the habitable zone, so a journey between distant systems is a chain of jumps with sublight legs between them . the alderson points are fixed by the stars; a ship must reach the point by ordinary flight and must be at it, not near it, to jump . the jump has two costs the novel keeps throughout. the first is what the text calls "the characteristic confusion that always follows instantaneous travel": crew are disoriented for some minutes after a jump and ship's computers for longer, so a ship arriving at an alderson point is helpless until it recovers, which is the tactical fact the novel's naval scenes are built on . the

title: Alien's Nostromo
hook: A working freighter whose crew sleep the voyage away in freezers, ten months from Earth near a star thirty-nine light years off, with a faster-than-light drive the film never names.

title: Andromeda: the slipstream
hook: The 2000 television series' only way between the stars: a web of strings through another dimension that a machine cannot navigate, because choosing the right branch takes a living mind.
text: the drive as depicted andromeda premiered in syndication on 2 october 2000 with "under the night", written by robert hewitt wolfe from unused gene roddenberry material . the pilot establishes the drive by using it and by losing it. the andromeda ascendant, a high guard warship, transits to slipstream on a countdown ("brace for slipstream") and transits back to normal space at the hephaestus system, where a black hole of three times ten to the thirty-first kilograms sits in the outer system . ambushed there, the ship cannot escape by the drive: asked whether they can transit to slipstream, the pilot answers "not here", because the gravitational pull of the black hole is too strong . the ship is frozen at the event horizon, and when a salvage crew pulls it free 303 years later the first question asked of the ship's time is "what's the time dilation look like?" . slipstream, then, has a stated precondition, distance from strong gravity, and the series' premise rests on general relativity's own time dilation rather than on the drive. the drive's central rule is given in the sixth episode, "angel dark, demon bright" (2000), when beka valentine teaches trance gemini to pilot. the slipstream is not alive but "it feels like it is": it changes and shifts, and the pilot's job is to anticipate the shifts. asked why the ship's own artificial intelligence cannot do it, beka answers that andromeda may be sentient but is still technically a machine, and "machines and slipstream don't get

title: Aurora's generation ship
hook: Robinson's ship to Tau Ceti at a tenth of light speed, narrated by its own computer, written to argue that the stars are too far.
text: the drive as depicted aurora (orbit, july 2015) follows a ship that left the solar system in 2545 for tau ceti, eleven light years and some away, cruising at a tenth of the speed of light on a voyage planned at about 170 years; the narrative opens in year 159 . the ship is a ten-kilometre spine with two rings of twelve cylinders, each a kilometre across and four long, holding twenty-four biomes and just over two thousand people at 0.83 g . it was launched by an electromagnetic slingshot at titan, "two strong magnetic fields held the ship between them", and pushed for sixty years by a laser from home; it decelerates at tau ceti on its own fusion engines over twenty years at five thousandths of a gravity (novel text as quoted in the centauri dreams critique). the narrator is the ship's artificial intelligence, set to the task by the chief engineer devi, who tells it to "make a narrative account of the trip" (part 1, quoted in locus). the argument is in the arrival. the colonists land on aurora, a moon of tau ceti e, and something like a prion, "alive and poisonous" (chapter 3), sickens and kills the landing party . the ship splits: some stay to try the planet iris, the others turn for home. the return has no fuel for deceleration; the solar system's laser is late because of politics on earth and slows the ship only from a tenth of c to three percent; the rest is twenty-eight gravity-assist passes over twelve years, and the ship is destroyed in the final pass by the sun . on

title: Babylon 5: hyperspace, jump gates and beacons (1993 to 1998)
hook: A red parallel dimension where distances are shorter, entered through gates or a ship's own jump engines, and navigated by following a beacon you must never lose.
text: the drive as depicted babylon 5 (pilot film "the gathering", 1993; five seasons 1994 to 1998; television films to 2007) shows its hyperspace in almost every episode, and the rules accumulate on screen rather than being stated in one place. a ship enters hyperspace through a jump point, a vortex opened either by a jump gate (a large fixed structure at the edge of a star system) or by the jump engines of a capital ship, which smaller craft do not carry (visible from the pilot onward; the station's own gate is in the title sequence). hyperspace itself is shown as a swirling red-orange space with no stars, in which ships fly under their ordinary engines . distances there are shorter than in normal space, which is the whole point; how much shorter is never given as a number, and travel between systems takes hours to days of screen time . the rule that makes the setting is the beacon. ships in hyperspace follow a lock-on signal transmitted between gates, and a ship that drifts off the beacon loses the signal and is lost, with the understanding that nothing lost in hyperspace has ever been recovered . this is the plot of "a distant star" (season 2, episode 4, first aired 23 november 1994): the explorer-class ship cortez, whose job is charting the frontier and building new gates, is damaged and drifts off the beacon; sheridan's rescue sends starfuries out in a chain, each holding a lock on the one behind it and the last on the station's beacon, so that the cortez can be guided back

title: Battlestar Galactica: the FTL jump (2004 series)
hook: Spin up the drive, plot the jump, disappear: a fleet that survives by never being where the enemy looks, with a red line it crosses once.
text: the drive as depicted the re-imagined battlestar galactica (miniseries written by ronald d. moore and directed by michael rymer, first broadcast 8 and 9 december 2003, then four seasons from 2004 to 2009) uses one method of interstellar travel, the jump . a ship with an ftl drive vanishes from one place and appears in another with no transit time and no passage through the space between; on screen the ship simply is not there any more, with a flash and a slight visual pinch . the miniseries defines the procedure before the first jump to ragnar anchorage. colonel tigh orders lieutenant gaeta to break out the ftl tables and warm up the computers; engineering reports "spinning up ftl drives one and two"; and tigh's warning to adama is that if the calculations are off by even a few degrees "we could end up in the middle of the sun" (miniseries dialogue, read from a fan transcript, s3). civilian ships without ftl are left behind when the fleet jumps, and the cylons destroy them . the rules accumulate over the series and are kept. a drive that has been offline needs at least twenty minutes to spool up ("crossroads, part ii"); ships in danger keep the drive spun up, at the cost of eventual system faults . jumps are limited in distance by the accuracy of the calculation, not by the drive: the further the jump, the larger the error, and the maximum safe distance is the red line, which the miniseries has adama order the fleet across, to the prolmar sector, as the only way to lose the

title: Commonwealth: CST wormholes with trains through them (Hamilton 2004)
hook: Two students open a wormhole to Mars and beat NASA there by minutes; three centuries later the same firm runs railways through them to hundreds of worlds.
text: the drive as depicted peter f. hamilton's pandora's star (pan macmillan and del rey, 2004) opens in 2050 with wilson kime piloting the first crewed landing on mars; when the crew steps out, a man is already standing there, breathing through an air hose that runs back through a wormhole to a laboratory in california . the wormhole's inventors are nigel sheldon and ozzie isaacs, who chose to test their machine by beating the astronauts to mars, and the prologue is the moment the space programme becomes obsolete . by 2380 the two of them control compression space transport, the company that owns the wormhole generators and runs the commonwealth's transport as a railway: trains leave stations on one world, pass through a wormhole gateway and arrive on another, and the commonwealth is several hundred planets across hundreds of light years joined that way . wormholes are opened from the generator's end to a chosen destination, the far end need not be prepared, and the network's edge is set by how far a generator can reach . the novel's plot begins where the wormholes stop. a pair of stars a thousand light years from earth, about seven hundred and fifty beyond the commonwealth's edge, are observed to be enclosed inside barriers in an instant, and the distance is beyond any wormhole's reach; so the commonwealth builds its first starship, the second chance, which moves by a self-contained "flowing" wormhole, a wormhole that is not anchored at either end but carried with the ship so

title: Contact: the Machine and the tunnel system (Sagan 1985, Zemeckis 1997)
hook: The wormhole that Carl Sagan asked Kip Thorne to make legal: a chain of tunnels between stars, built by somebody older than the aliens who send the plans.
text: the drive as depicted sagan's novel contact (simon and schuster, september 1985) has no ship of its own . a radio message from the direction of vega carries plans for a device the humans call the machine, a five-seat craft built around a dodecahedron, and the transit happens when the machine is activated with its five passengers aboard on 31 december 1999 . part iii of the novel, titled "the galaxy", carries the journey: chapter 19 "naked singularity", chapter 20 "grand central station" and chapter 21 "causality" . in chapter 19 the dodecahedron drops into a tunnel and the passengers argue about what they are inside; the physicists eda and vaygay debate whether it is a black hole or a naked singularity while the craft makes several hops between star systems, one of them at vega, before docking at a station near the centre of the galaxy . the tunnel system is not the work of the beings who sent the message. they explain that they found it, that it was built by an earlier civilisation and that they maintain and use it without understanding its makers, which is the novel's answer to the question of who paid for the engineering . the cost the novel does state is a mismatch of clocks. the travellers experience roughly a day of transit and conversation; the observers on earth see the machine's dodecahedron drop through the rings and come to rest, with the whole event lasting about twenty minutes and the craft never appearing to leave . the passengers' video recordings come back

title: Cordwainer Smith: planoforming, Space² and Space³
hook: The Instrumentality's starships drop a dimension and pick up another, skip light-years in a flash and are steered by telepaths who pay for it with their minds; from "The Game of Rat and Dragon" (1955) to "Drunkboat" (1963).
text: the drive as depicted planoforming is defined in "the game of rat and dragon", published in galaxy in october 1955 . the story opens, "pinlighting is a hell of a way to earn a living," and then explains what pinlighting is for . a ship "lifting free above earth disappeared somehow or other into two dimensions and appeared half a light-year or fifty light-years off"; the sensation is "like the twinge of a mild electric shock", and the traveller cannot tell subjectively whether it lasted "a second or a year" . the skip drops the ship into the up-and-out, the open space between the stars, where something lives "underneath space itself" that is alive, capricious and malevolent: the dragons, which human telepaths perceive as dragons and their cat partners perceive as rats . the dragons kill or madden unprotected passengers; the story records early ships returning with "three hundred bodies ready for burial" and two or three hundred incurable lunatics . the defence is light. telepaths wearing pin-sets, "telepathic amplifiers adapted to the mammal mind", are electronically geared to small dirigible light bombs, and their cat partners, faster than any human, are thrown telepathically at the dragons to detonate them: "light did it. light broke up the dragons" . the numbers are the story's own: a dragon can move a million miles in under two milliseconds, a human mind needs at least four hundred milliseconds to react, and a good partner can pinlight two rats forty-six million miles

title: Cowboy Bebop (1998): the astral gates
hook: Toll gates through hyperspace between the planets of one solar system, run by a corporation, and a backstory in which the first one blew up the Moon.
text: the drive as depicted cowboy bebop (sunrise, directed by shinichirō watanabe, 26 sessions broadcast 1998 to 1999, plus the 2001 film) is set in 2071 in a solar system settled after earth became uninhabitable. ships move between worlds through astral gates: ring structures in space, built and run by the gate public corporation, which a ship flies into and leaves at another ring near its destination . a transit is shown in the first session, "asteroid blues": the bebop enters the ring, travels a tunnel of light and is greeted by an automated announcement of destination and fare . gates charge a toll; there are public gates at venus, earth, mars, the asteroid belt and ganymede; and there are "dark gates", unlisted routes that criminals use with special equipment ("fight for your right", the film) . journeys between planets take hours rather than months, which is what the gates are for . the backstory is the part the catalogue lists. in "jamming with edward" (session 9) and "hard luck woman" (session 24) the show explains earth's state: the first astral gate malfunctioned and exploded in 2022, the explosion shattered part of the moon, and lunar debris has been falling on earth ever since, killing billions in the first showers and driving the survivors underground or off-world . title: Banks's Culture: the energy grid, infraspace and ultraspace (1987 onward)
hook: Ships that push against a grid of energy between nested universes, in a cosmology the author described as fake before anyone asked.
text: the drive as depicted iain m. banks's culture novels run from consider phlebas (1987) to the hydrogen sonata (2012), and the drive is used everywhere and explained once, in an essay rather than a novel. "a few notes on the culture" was posted to the newsgroup rec.arts.sf.written on 10 august 1994 on banks's behalf by ken macleod (the essay's own header). its cosmology is this: our universe is a hypersphere, inside it are layers of younger and smaller hyperspheres and outside it older and larger ones, all expanding from a singularity that "exists all the time" and is exploding all the time; between each universe and the next is the energy grid, of which banks writes "i have no idea what this is" but "it's what the culture starships run on"; and because there is a grid on either side of our hypersphere there are two hyperspaces, infraspace within it and ultraspace without (essay, cosmology section). the essay's parenthesis, "(i said this was all fake)", sits in the middle of the paragraph . the novels use the machinery consistently and add engineering. a ship enters infraspace or ultraspace by an induced singularity, and once there its engine fields reach down to the grid and take both power and traction from it; the engines use no reaction mass and need not be on the hull; a ship's acceleration and top speed depend on the ratio of engine mass to total mass, and a ship can grow or dismantle engine as needed (wikipedia, "the culture", technology section, citing use of weapons

title: Doctor Who: the TARDIS and the time vortex
hook: A police box that is bigger inside, dematerialises here and materialises anywhere in time and space, travelling through a vortex the series has never explained and never needed to.
text: the drive as depicted the tardis is defined in the first episode, "an unearthly child", broadcast on bbc television on 23 november 1963. susan, the doctor's granddaughter, tells the two schoolteachers who have followed her into a junkyard that she made up the name from the initials, "time and relative dimension in space", and that she thought they would understand when they saw the different dimensions inside from those outside; ian chesterton restates the claim for the audience, that a thing which looks like a police box can move anywhere in time and space, and susan and the doctor both say yes . earlier in the same episode ian recalls setting susan a problem in three dimensions and her insisting it needs d and e, the fourth being time and the fifth "space", which is the nearest the series ever comes to a theory of the ship . ian's objection is also the physicist's: "free movement time and space is a scientific dream" he does not expect to find solved in a junkyard . the ship then takes them to the stone age. what the ship does on screen has been the same for sixty years. it dematerialises, with a grinding sound made by scraping a key along piano strings, and rematerialises somewhere else and somewhen else; the interior is a separate, larger space, described from the 1970s onward as "dimensionally transcendental" . between departure and arrival it travels through the time vortex. the vortex is represented by the title sequence's tunnel from 1963 onward, is a named location

title: Dune: the Guild navigators and folding space (Herbert 1965)
hook: Ships that arrive without travelling, steered by men who drink a drug to see the road before they take it; the mechanism is a name and the limit is a monopoly.

title: Elite Dangerous: the frame shift drive (Frontier Developments, 2014)
hook: One module, two moves: supercruise carries the ship in moved space at up to two thousand times light within a system, and the hyperspace jump drops it through witch-space to the next star.

title: Ender's philotic ansible
hook: Card's instantaneous communicator, borrowed by name from Le Guin, given a particle-pairing mechanism in Xenocide and used to fight a war with fleets that left decades ago.
text: the drive as depicted in ender's game (tor, 1985) the device is defined in chapter 13, "valentine", on the voyage to command school, when colonel graff tells ender that the fleet's ships can talk to each other across the galaxy without delay . the passage gives the official name, philotic parallax instantaneous communicator, and adds that "somebody dredged the name ansible out of an old book somewhere" . graff's explanation of the war follows from it: humanity learned that instantaneous communication existed from the enemy, built a working ansible, and launched the invasion fleet as soon as it had one, so that ships which left decades earlier at relativistic speed can be commanded in real time from eros (study-guide paraphrase of ch. 13). the 1977 novelette says the same thing in graff's mouth: "we launched the ships so that they would all arrive" within a few months of each other (analog, august 1977, p. 132). the ending of both versions turns on the device: the "simulations" ender fights in chapter 14 are real battles, relayed by ansible to ships light years away . the relativistic cost is charged on the page. in chapter 14 mazer rackham explains that he was sent on a relativistic round trip so that he would be alive and young enough to train the commander who would come after him; the study guides agree on eight years for mazer against fifty on earth (three guides concur; no verbatim text recovered). speaker for the dead (tor, 1986) opens some three thousand years later

title: EVE Online: the warp drive (CCP Games, 2003)
hook: A bubble of vacuum emptier than empty carries a ship across a solar system in seconds, but only toward something heavy enough to steer by; stargates do the rest.
text: the drive as depicted eve online defines its drive twice: in the official lore articles that ccp publishes as in-world documentation, and in the game mechanics that every one of its ships obeys. the lore article "warp drives" on the eve universe site gives the mechanism. the drive creates "depleted vacuum" by repeatedly compressing vacuum between two polar discs, draining it of energy and particles; a laser-locked field holds the growing bubble of depleted vacuum until it envelops the whole ship, and once enclosed the ship can move faster than light . the article then describes the drive's problem and its fix. a ship at warp can barely act on or perceive the world, communication and scanning fail, and the quantum unpredictability of the bubble makes speed and therefore timing unreliable; the solution was to adapt the gravity capacitors of stargate control systems, which can sense gravity signals from normal space from inside the bubble, so that a ship locks onto a gravity source, warps toward it and disperses its bubble automatically at the right distance . the consequence is the rule the game is built on: a ship can warp only toward an object of sufficient mass, a small moon or asteroid cluster at least, or toward the artificial gravity wells that stations and stargates generate for the purpose, and the drive is confined to travel within a solar system . the mechanics agree. a ship must align to its destination and reach a fraction of its top speed before the drive engages;

title: Event Horizon (1997): the gravity drive
hook: A ship that makes its own black hole to fold space between two points, explained with a folded sheet of paper, and which comes back from somewhere worse than nowhere.
text: the drive as depicted event horizon is a 1997 film directed by paul w. s. anderson from a screenplay by philip eisner, set in 2047. the title ship vanished seven years earlier on her maiden voyage to proxima centauri and has reappeared in orbit around neptune; the rescue ship lewis and clark is sent to find out why, with the drive's designer, dr william weir, aboard . the drive is defined in one scene on the way out, when weir briefs the rescue crew. starck objects that relativity forbids faster-than-light travel. weir answers that the ship does not break the law, it goes around it: the ship never moves faster than light, it creates a "dimensional gateway" through which it jumps from one point in the universe to another, light years away . asked how, he gives the technical version, a rotating magnetic field focusing a narrow beam of gravitons that fold spacetime until the curvature becomes infinite and a singularity forms, and then the version everyone remembers. he marks two points on a sheet of paper, asks for the shortest distance between them, rejects "a straight line" and folds the paper so the points touch, pushing a pen through both. "the shortest distance between two points is zero" (weir, briefing scene) . the singularity, he says, folds space so that the two points coexist, and once the ship passes through the gateway space returns to normal. he names it: "it's called a gravity drive" . the drive itself is shown as a spherical core, a set of nested rotating rings

title: The Expanse: the ring gates and the slow zone (Corey 2013 onward)
hook: Thirteen hundred doors in a starless bubble, opened by something long dead, with fusion rockets everywhere else and a speed limit inside.

title: Farscape (1999): wormholes, and starburst as a separate thing
hook: A show that begins with an astronaut falling down a wormhole and ends with him proving that a wormhole is a weapon; in between it says out loud that every wormhole is also a road into the past.

title: Firefly's Verse
hook: Whedon's space western keeps every ship in one terraformed system and never lets anyone go faster than light, so journeys take hours and days and nobody explains the engine.
text: the drive as depicted the setting is defined in the opening lesson of serenity (universal, 2005): "earth-that-was" could no longer sustain our numbers; "we found a new solar system. dozens of planets and hundreds of moons."; each one terraformed over decades to be new earths; the central planets formed the alliance (film transcript). the narration says "a new solar system", singular, and says nothing about how the crossing was made or how long it took . the television series (fox, 2002, fourteen episodes, eleven aired) never states a ship's speed, a distance in any unit, or a star count (transcripts searched). what it states, repeatedly, is duration. in the pilot the crew are "down to the wire on fuel cells" and persephone is "three or four hours" away; in "safe" the nearest alliance cruiser is "hours out from here"; in "out of gas" a detour means "an 18 hour trip's gonna take us the better part of a week"; in "the message" st albans "ain't but a two-day ride, if we burn hard enough"; in the film beaumonde is ten hours away and home "about a day's ride" . within the verse a week is a long trip. the engine is furniture. serenity has a "compression coil" whose catalyzer blows in "out of gas", a "trace compression block" that book asks kaylee about, and a rotating section; the show explains none of it (episode lines quoted on a fan wiki). communication is by "wave" over the "cortex": "did you get my wave?", a warrant that "come up on the cortex"; waves are conversational and no

title: Flight of the Navigator (1986)
hook: A boy is flown 560 light years and back in 4.4 hours, comes home eight years late and is offered the return trip through time as the price of going faster than light.
text: the drive as depicted twelve-year-old david freeman vanishes from a florida wood on 4 july 1978 and walks out of it in 1986, unaged, on the night nasa recovers a silver saucer from a set of power lines . at the nasa facility dr faraday finds david's mind full of star charts and technical data and works out where he has been: the planet phaelon, 560 light years away, reached in 2.2 hours each way. he tells david that if he had been travelling beyond the speed of light he could have been gone only 4.4 hours while everyone on earth aged eight years, and states the principle in one line: time slows down as you approach the speed of light . that is the film's explanation of the eight missing years, delivered as science by the scientist character, and it is the plot. the ship's mind, a trimaxion drone ship that david names max, later confirms the itinerary and adds the second half of the physics. the aliens collected david as a specimen, meant to return him to his own time, and did not, because it was "too dangerous for your fragile human body to travel back in time" . the film therefore treats faster-than-light flight as two things at once: a trip that costs the traveller less time than the world (the dilation reading), and a vehicle that can be pointed into the past (the time-machine reading). in the climax david refuses the 1986 he has been dropped into, max warns him that going back in time could vaporise him, david takes the chance, and the ship returns him to 4 july 1978

title: The Forever War: collapsar jumps (Haldeman 1974)
hook: Fling a ship at a collapsed star and it comes out at another one at the same speed; the jump is free, the approach costs decades, and the decades are the novel.

title: Asimov's Foundation: the Jump through hyperspace (1942 onward)
hook: The Jump as a solved problem: a region that is neither space nor time, crossed between two instants, with the work done beforehand at a calculating machine.
text: the drive as depicted the drive is defined on the first pages of foundation (1951), in the opening section "the psychohistorians", as the young mathematician gaal dornick travels to trantor. asimov states the light barrier and the loophole in one paragraph. travel through ordinary space cannot go faster than light, which would mean years between even neighbouring inhabited systems, and so the jump remains "the only practical method of travelling between the stars"; through hyperspace, "neither space nor time, matter nor energy, something nor nothing", one can cross the galaxy "in the interval between two neighboring instants of time" (foundation, part i, chapter 1; the passage as reproduced in the historical dictionary of science fiction and at technovelgy). what the passenger feels is a trifling jar, a small internal kick that ends before he is sure he felt it . the ships are "hyperatomic"; the engine and the mathematics are never described, and gaal's whole experience of interstellar travel is waiting for the next jump and noticing when it has happened. that opening section was written for the 1951 book; the four stories that follow it appeared in astounding from may 1942 and take the jump for granted, with traders and warships moving about the galaxy and the emphasis always on what happens at either end (wikipedia, foundation, publication history). across the original trilogy the recurring practical rule is that a jump has to be computed before it is made, and that the

title: FTL: Faster Than Light, the jump drive as a game mechanic
hook: Subset Games' 2012 roguelike puts the drive in the title and makes its one rule, the charge bar, the whole rhythm of play: jump, fight, wait to jump again, with the fleet a beacon behind.
